docs.title: Fayde
docs.text:
Fayde finds the stars in a FITS image, matches them against a star catalog, and returns a world coordinate system (WCS) solution with its measured accuracy. It runs from the command line and from Python on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

Fayde is developed and maintained by Shane Ryall.

To solve your first image, follow these pages in order:

  1. Install Fayde.
  2. Choose and connect a star catalog.
  3. Solve a frame.

docs.title: Get the UCAC4 catalog
docs.text:
Fayde reads the UCAC4 catalog (Zacharias et al. 2013) from a local copy of its original binary files. Fayde doesn't include the catalog. The Strasbourg astronomical Data Center (CDS) publishes it as catalog I/322A. The download is about 8.9 GB.

Use a terminal on Linux or macOS, or PowerShell on Windows. On Windows, use curl.exe in place of curl in the download commands.

To download the catalog, follow these steps:

  1. On Linux or macOS, create the catalog directories:
mkdir -p UCAC4/u4b UCAC4/u4i

On Windows, create the directories:

mkdir UCAC4\u4b, UCAC4\u4i
  1. Go to the u4b directory:
cd UCAC4/u4b
  1. Download the 900 zone files, z001 to z900:
curl -fO "https://vizier.cfa.harvard.edu/ftp/cats/I/322A/UCAC4/u4b/z[001-900]"

If the download stops, start it again from the file that was downloading. For example, if it stopped at z412, change the range to z[412-900].

  1. Go to the u4i directory:
cd ../u4i
  1. Download the two index files:
curl -fO "https://vizier.cfa.harvard.edu/ftp/cats/I/322A/UCAC4/u4i/{u4index.unf,u4hpm.dat}"

Fayde uses u4index.unf to seek directly to the stars that it needs and u4hpm.dat for the proper motions of fast-moving stars. If u4index.unf is missing, Fayde finds the same stars by searching each zone file.

  1. Return to the directory where you started:
cd ../..
  1. On Linux or macOS, count the zone files:
ls UCAC4/u4b | wc -l

On Windows, count the zone files:

(Get-ChildItem UCAC4\u4b).Count

Check that the output is 900. If it's lower, download the missing files again.

The catalog directory has this layout:

UCAC4/
├── u4b/
│   ├── z001
│   ├── ...
│   └── z900
└── u4i/
    ├── u4hpm.dat
    └── u4index.unf

When a Fayde command has a --ucac4 option, give it the path to the UCAC4 directory, which is the directory that contains u4b. Download all 900 zone files, because Fayde reports an error when a zone that it needs is missing.

To leave out --ucac4, set the FAYDE_UCAC4 environment variable to the path to the UCAC4 directory. For more information about this variable, see Set the catalog directory once.

docs.title: Pattern indexes for sub-degree fields
docs.text:
A pattern index lets Fayde solve a frame when the pointing or pixel scale is uncertain or unknown. If you know the pointing and have a precise pixel scale from a frame header or instrument profile, you need only the UCAC4 catalog.

An index covers fields near its target field of view. Fayde chooses among the indexes you provide. To cover a wider range of scales, follow these steps:

  1. Build an index for each field of view.
  2. Pass each index to fayde solve with a separate --index option.

docs.title: Build the recommended indexes
docs.text:
The two recommended indexes cover the whole sky at epoch 2025.0, for fields of about 1° and somewhat wider. You need the full UCAC4 catalog, with all 900 zone files, and at least 32 GB of free memory.

Replace UCAC4_DIR with the path to the directory that contains u4b. To cover both field sizes, build both indexes:

  1. Build the index for fields of about 1°:
fayde index build --ucac4 UCAC4_DIR --fov 1.0 --stars-per-fov 23.7 --pattern-stars-per-fov 23.7 --mag-limit 15.5 --min-edge 0.04 --epoch 2025 -o allsky-1.0.fidx
  1. Build the index for fields somewhat wider than 1°:
fayde index build --ucac4 UCAC4_DIR --fov 1.3 --stars-per-fov 40 --pattern-stars-per-fov 20 --stars-per-field 12 --mag-limit 15.5 --min-edge 0.05 --epoch 2025 -o allsky-1.3.fidx

The builds used the version 0.1.0 binary on a 32-core x86_64 Linux computer. The table lists the build results:

Index Stars Patterns File size Build time Peak memory allsky-1.0.fidx 1,572,824 259,900,180 17.2 GB 30 min 26 s 22.7 GB allsky-1.3.fidx 1,572,824 153,951,343 10.2 GB 21 min 50 s 13.6 GB

docs.title: Plan for memory
docs.text:
Fayde loads the entire index into memory. On an otherwise idle 64-bit Arm computer, fayde index info loaded each recommended index with these results:

Index Load time Peak memory allsky-1.0.fidx 48 s 18.3 GB allsky-1.3.fidx 27 s 10.9 GB

The fayde command loads the index each time that it runs. To solve many frames, use the Python package and reuse one fayde.Solver, which loads the index once.

docs.title: Check a content hash
docs.text:
Each index has a content hash, a 64-bit checksum that covers its stars, patterns, and build options. Fayde uses the hash to identify the index that produced a solution and detect file damage. The hash isn't a cryptographic signature. Fayde records each index's hash in the identity.indexes[].content_hash field of the solve report.

To compare your index with the expected hash, follow these steps:

  1. Print the index metadata:
fayde index info allsky-1.0.fidx
  1. Compare the content_hash field in the output with the following table.

An index's bytes and hash don't depend on the platform or build profile. Fayde uses fayde_core::Portable for all its math. Builds from the full UCAC4 catalog with the commands on this page produce these hashes:

Index content_hash allsky-1.0.fidx 1ddf14fa50ad59dd allsky-1.3.fidx 4ad74722223054e1

Version 0.1.0 and every later version build the same bytes. If a release changes the bytes, the release notes describe the change, and this page lists the new hashes.

Continuous integration doesn't build the recommended indexes, because each one takes tens of gigabytes of memory and about half an hour.

docs.title: Index build options
docs.text:
To list every option and its default value, run fayde index build --help. The table describes the options used in the recommended commands, and --region:

Option Meaning --fov The field of view that the index is built for, in degrees --stars-per-fov The number of stars kept per field of view, selected uniformly over HEALPix cells --pattern-stars-per-fov The number of those stars, taken brightest first, that form patterns --stars-per-field The number of stars per lattice field from which patterns are formed --mag-limit The faintest magnitude considered --min-edge The shortest pattern edge, in degrees. Below it, centroid errors dominate --epoch The epoch that the star positions are propagated to, as a Julian year --region RA,DEC,RADIUS Builds a regional index instead of an all-sky index, with RA, DEC, and RADIUS in degrees. A regional build takes minutes, which makes it useful for tests

For more information about the algorithms, see References.

docs.title: Install Fayde
docs.text: Use pip install to install both the Python module and the fayde command. To use the command without Python, install the command-line tool on its own. Then get the UCAC4 catalog.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
To install Fayde, use a computer that runs one of these systems:

  • Linux on x86_64 or 64-bit Arm, with glibc 2.17 or later
  • macOS 11 or later, on Apple silicon or an Intel processor
  • Windows 10 or later, on x86_64

You also need the following:

  • About 9 GB of free disk space for the UCAC4 catalog
  • For the Python package, CPython 3.10 or later

To solve a frame, you also need a FITS image from your own observation. The image must meet these requirements:

  • Fayde measures point stars, straight trails that share a length and direction, and some curved trails. A shared curved path or field rotation can use a template learned from the image. For the detection modes and how to read the result, see Detect stars without solving.
  • The image isn't compressed with fpack. To decompress an image, use the funpack program from CFITSIO.
  • The header gives the pointing and the pixel scale. If it doesn't, you can specify them yourself.

docs.title: Install the command-line tool
docs.text: Each release includes a prebuilt fayde binary. You don't need Rust to install it. After you install the tool, continue to Get the UCAC4 catalog.

docs.title: Install on Linux or macOS
docs.text:
To install the latest release, follow these steps:

  1. In a terminal, identify your operating system and processor architecture:
uname -sm
  1. Set the platform variable to the value that matches the output:
Output of uname -sm Value Linux x86_64 linux-x86_64 Linux aarch64 linux-aarch64 Darwin arm64 macos-arm64 Darwin x86_64 macos-x86_64

For example, for the output Darwin arm64, set the variable to macos-arm64:

platform=macos-arm64
  1. Download the archive:
curl -LO "https://github.com/shaneryall/Fayde/releases/latest/download/fayde-$platform.tar.gz"

Optional: Before you extract the archive, check it as described in Verify a download.

  1. Extract the archive:
tar -xzf "fayde-$platform.tar.gz"

Extraction creates a directory named fayde- followed by your platform value. The directory contains the fayde binary, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, the license files (LICENSE, NOTICE, and THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md), and CITATION.cff. It also contains the documentation pages in its docs directory and the example instrument profile in its profiles directory.

  1. Install the binary in /usr/local/bin, which is on your PATH:
sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/bin && sudo install -m 755 "fayde-$platform/fayde" /usr/local/bin/fayde

If sudo prompts for your password, enter it.

  1. If macOS blocks a binary that you downloaded with a web browser instead of curl, remove the quarantine attribute to allow it to run:
sudo xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /usr/local/bin/fayde
  1. Check the installation:
fayde --version

The output is similar to the following:

fayde 0.3.0 (0123456789ab)

docs.title: Install on Windows
docs.text:
To install the latest release, follow these steps:

  1. In PowerShell, download the archive:
curl.exe -LO https://github.com/shaneryall/Fayde/releases/latest/download/fayde-windows-x86_64.zip

Optional: Before you extract the archive, check it as described in Verify a download.

  1. Extract the archive:
Expand-Archive fayde-windows-x86_64.zip -DestinationPath .

Extraction creates a directory named fayde-windows-x86_64. The directory contains fayde.exe, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, the license files (LICENSE, NOTICE, and THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md), and CITATION.cff. It also contains the documentation pages in its docs directory and the example instrument profile in its profiles directory.

  1. In the current PowerShell session, add the extracted directory to Path:
$env:Path += ";$PWD\fayde-windows-x86_64"

The Path change lasts until you close PowerShell.

  1. Check the installation:
fayde --version

The output is similar to the following:

fayde 0.3.0 (0123456789ab)

Optional: To keep the Path change after you close PowerShell, follow these steps:

  1. In the Windows search box, enter environment variables.
  2. Select Edit environment variables for your account.
  3. Select Path.
  4. Click Edit.
  5. Click New.
  6. Enter the full path of the extracted directory.
  7. Click OK.

docs.title: Verify a download
docs.text:
Each release includes a SHA256SUMS file that lists the SHA-256 checksum of every other file in the release.

To check an archive on Linux or macOS, follow these steps:

  1. In the directory that contains the archive, download the checksum file:
curl -LO https://github.com/shaneryall/Fayde/releases/latest/download/SHA256SUMS
  1. Compare the checksums. On Linux, use sha256sum:
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS

On macOS, use shasum:

shasum -a 256 --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS

The output names the archive, followed by OK.

To check the archive on Windows, follow these steps:

  1. In PowerShell, in the directory that contains the archive, download the checksum file:
curl.exe -LO https://github.com/shaneryall/Fayde/releases/latest/download/SHA256SUMS
  1. Print the checksum of the archive:
(Get-FileHash fayde-windows-x86_64.zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
  1. Print the expected checksum:
Select-String fayde-windows-x86_64.zip SHA256SUMS
  1. Compare the checksums from the two outputs. The archive is intact when they match. Uppercase and lowercase letters are equivalent.

A checksum shows that the archive is intact. Releases from 0.3.3 on also have a build attestation, which shows that a GitHub Actions workflow of the Fayde repository built the archive.

Optional: To check the attestation, use the GitHub CLI in the directory that contains the archive:

gh attestation verify ARCHIVE --repo shaneryall/Fayde

Replace ARCHIVE with the archive's filename, for example fayde-linux-x86_64.tar.gz. The command fails if no attestation from the Fayde repository matches the archive.

docs.title: Install with Cargo
docs.text:
You need Rust 1.85 or later to build the fayde command from crates.io. To build and install the command, follow these steps:

  1. In a terminal, install the fayde-cli crate:
cargo install --locked fayde-cli

Cargo installs fayde in its binary directory, which is ~/.cargo/bin unless you changed it. If your shell can't find fayde, add that directory to your PATH.

  1. Check the installation:
fayde --version

A build from crates.io shows unknown in place of the commit. The output is similar to the following:

fayde 0.3.0 (unknown)

docs.title: Install the Python package
docs.text:
The fayde package on PyPI includes a prebuilt wheel for every supported platform. Each wheel supports CPython 3.10 and every later version, and you don't need Rust to install it. The package installs both the Python module and the fayde command.

If PyPI has no wheel for your platform, pip builds the package from its source distribution. You need Rust 1.85 or later for that build.

To install the package, follow these steps:

  1. On Linux or macOS, in a terminal, create a virtual environment:
python3 -m venv .venv

On Debian and Ubuntu, this command needs the python3-venv package.

On Windows, in PowerShell, create the virtual environment:

py -m venv .venv
  1. On Linux or macOS, activate the virtual environment:
source .venv/bin/activate

On Windows, activate the virtual environment:

.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

If PowerShell reports that running scripts is disabled, follow these steps:

  1. Allow scripts for the current session:

    Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned

  2. Activate the environment again.

  3. Install the package:

python -m pip install fayde
  1. Check the installation:
python -c "import fayde; print(fayde.__version__)"

The output is the version number, for example 0.3.0.

  1. Check that you can run the fayde command:
fayde --version

The output is similar to the following:

fayde 0.3.0 (0123456789ab)

The command is available while the virtual environment is active.

To solve a frame from Python, see Use Fayde from Python.

docs.title: Use Fayde from Python
docs.text:
To install the package, see Install the Python package.

To open the catalog and load the indexes only once, reuse one solver for every frame. To find the stars in an image and solve it, create the solver and call solve_image:

import fayde

solver = fayde.Solver("/path/to/UCAC4")
report = solver.solve_image("frame.fits")
if report["solved"]:
    cards = report["wcs_cards"]

Replace /path/to/UCAC4 with the path to your catalog directory and frame.fits with the path to your FITS image. If the FAYDE_UCAC4 environment variable contains the path to the catalog directory, you can omit the catalog argument: fayde.Solver().

The image argument accepts the path to a FITS file, a 2-D NumPy array, or an Astropy HDU. For an array, pass the frame's header with header. You can use Fayde without NumPy or Astropy.

If you detect the stars yourself, pass their positions to solve. In this example, x, y, and flux are sequences of the source positions and fluxes from your detector, and hdr is the image header. The indexes and instrument arguments are optional. To solve the frame from these positions, check the WCS, fit the WCS again, and find catalog stars at the source positions, use these methods:

solver = fayde.Solver("/path/to/UCAC4", indexes=["allsky-1.0.fidx"])
report = solver.solve(x, y, flux=flux, header=hdr, instrument="profiles/example.json",
                      deadline=5.0)
if report["solved"]:
    cards = report["wcs_cards"]
    check = solver.verify(x, y, cards, header=hdr)
    refit = solver.refit(x, y, cards, header=hdr)
    stars = solver.stars_at(cards, x, y, header=hdr)

The verify method checks the WCS against the catalog without changing it. The refit method fits the WCS again from the matched stars. It returns the same report fields as solve, including wcs_cards when it finds a solution.

The solve, verify, and refit methods take x and y as 0-based positions, as NumPy and Astropy index pixels. If your positions are 1-based, as in FITS, pass origin=1. These methods also accept the following optional sequences, with one value for each source:

  • flux: The integrated flux in any linear unit
  • sigma_px: The 1σ position error in pixels
  • p_star: The prior probability that the source is a real star, from 0 to 1
  • truncated: Whether the frame edge or a mask cuts the source, as booleans or as 0 and 1

Fayde ignores sigma_px values that aren't positive and p_star values outside that range. In flux, sigma_px, and p_star, NaN means that the source has no value.

To find the stars in an image without solving it, use fayde.detect:

detection = fayde.detect("frame.fits")
sources = detection["sources"]

The x and y positions in the detection report are 1-based, as in FITS. To solve these sources, pass the report to solve_detection:

report = solver.solve_detection(detection, header=hdr)

The solve_detection method passes the image size and each source's position, flux, sigma_px, p_star, and truncated value to the solver. If the report identifies star trails, the method also passes the measured trail unless you give trail_length and trail_angle. It doesn't read the image header, so pass the header with header. If you pass the detection report's positions to solve without origin=1, Fayde interprets each coordinate as 1 pixel larger than its actual value.

If an image shows star trails in more than one direction, give the expected direction to fayde.detect with trail_angle, in degrees from +x toward +y. Fayde still measures the trail from the image. With solve_image, give trail_length and trail_angle together. The angle guides detection, and the two values replace the measured trail in the solve.

The Python interface follows the command line:

  • The solve, solve_detection, solve_image, verify, and refit methods take the command-line options under the same names with underscores, such as pointing_sigma and relax_priors_on_failure. In Python, run help(fayde) to list them. The detect function and the stars_at method have their own options. To list those options, run help(fayde.detect) and help(fayde.Solver.stars_at).
  • The solve_image method also takes the options of detect, such as detect_threshold, which must be at least 1.5.
  • Input coordinates x and y of solve, verify, refit, and stars_at are 0-based unless you pass origin=1. Pixel fields in the reports, including the source positions from detect, are 1-based, as in FITS and in the command-line report.
  • The header argument accepts a dictionary, a list of header cards, or an astropy.io.fits.Header. The WCS argument of verify, refit, and stars_at accepts the same types.
  • The instrument argument accepts a profile dictionary or the path to a profile file. The detect function also takes instrument or instrument_path. During detection, Fayde applies the profile's charge_transfer and periodic_pattern corrections. For more information, see Correct charge-transfer smear and Remove a periodic background pattern.
  • The report is a dictionary with the same fields as the command-line JSON report. For more information about these fields, see Read the report.
  • An invalid option raises ValueError. A solver failure raises fayde.FaydeError, which stores the report in its report attribute.
  • Fayde releases the global interpreter lock (GIL) while it solves, so threads can share one Solver.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
Every algorithm Fayde uses, where it comes from, and where it lives in the code. When an algorithm has no published source, the entry says so. The doc comment of the module that implements an algorithm cites the same source.

For a wider survey of the literature, with verdicts for Fayde, see Literature review.

Chem. 58, 1162 (1-D); Naidu & Fisher 1991, BMVC, doi:10.5244/C.5.28 (the "Gaussian estimator", bias compared with the parabola's); Anthony & Granick 2009, Langmuir 25, 8152 (2-D) Position, size, shape and amplitude of each source in closed form crates/fayde-detect/src/peaks.rs (measure) Least-squares quadratic surface on a 3 × 3 neighborhood (facet model) Haralick 1984, IEEE TPAMI 6(1), 58 The normal equations of that fit crates/fayde-detect/src/peaks.rs (measure) A matched filter followed by a 3 × 3 peak fit reaches the Cramér–Rao bound for well-sampled stars Vakili & Hogg 2016, arXiv:1610.05873 Why the cheap estimator is also the accurate one docs/design/detection.md §3.4 Cramér–Rao bound on a star's position: √2·σ/SNR background-limited, σ/√N source-limited King 1983, PASP 95, 163; Mendez, Silva & Lobos 2013, PASP 125, 580; Gaussian-weighted centroid (16/9)σ²/N: Mortensen et al. 2010, Nature Methods 7, 377, eq. 6 Check on the per-source position error crates/fayde-detect/src/lib.rs (finish), tests/synthetic.rs Line points from the Hessian of the smoothed image: direction along the eigenvector of the weaker curvature Steger 1998, IEEE TPAMI 20(2), 113; ratio of principal curvatures as an edge/ridge test: Lowe 2004, IJCV 60(2), 91, §4.1 Ridge-like peaks seed the streak tracer crates/fayde-detect/src/peaks.rs, streak.rs Streak model: a line segment convolved with a Gaussian; an end is where the profile falls to half Vereš et al. 2012, PASP 124, 1197 (arXiv:1209.6106) Streak ends at the half-level point; synthetic streaks crates/fayde-detect/src/streak.rs (fit), synth.rs Density of local maxima of a smoothed Gaussian noise field above a height: u·φ(u)/(4π σk²) for a Gaussian kernel Bond & Efstathiou 1987, MNRAS 226, 655, eq. A1.12; Cheng & Schwartzman 2017, Ann. Stat. 45(2), 529 (κ = 1 for a Gaussian kernel) Detection threshold from a false-alarm count; null model of p_star crates/fayde-detect/src/stats.rs (noise_peaks_above) Local false discovery rate: expected nulls over observed, per value Efron 2008, Stat. Sci. 23(1), 1; in astronomy: Miller et al. 2001, AJ 122, 3492 p_star of each source crates/fayde-detect/src/lib.rs (finish) Sharpness: light through the optics reaches a peak's neighbors, a hot pixel's charge does not Stetson 1987, PASP 99, 191 (DAOFIND's sharpness statistic); the test on the second faintest neighbor is Fayde's Hot pixels and cosmic rays crates/fayde-detect/src/lib.rs (sharp_in_raw) Moffat profile for seeing-limited stars Moffat 1969, A&A 3, 455 Synthetic test frames crates/fayde-detect/src/synth.rs FITS image arrays, BSCALE/BZERO/BLANK Pence et al. 2010, A&A 524, A42 (FITS Standard 3.0) §5.2, §4.4.2.5 Reading images for detection crates/fayde-fits/src/image.rs HEALPix NESTED pixelization Górski et al. 2005, ApJ 622, 759 Uniform star selection cells crates/fayde-index/src/healpix.rs Uniform catalog selection (N brightest separated stars per HEALPix cell; default 10″ separation, brighter replacements across cell boundaries) Lang et al. 2010, AJ 139, 1782 (astrometry.net uniformize-catalog); streaming replacement policy and 10″ default are Fayde choices Even dense-tier star density without close doubles occupying both slots crates/fayde-index/src/build.rs (Selector::push, select_stars) Fibonacci lattice on the sphere (golden angle reduced to one turn before sin/cos) González 2010, Math. Geosci. 42, 49 Pattern field centers crates/fayde-index/src/build.rs (lattice) 4-star patterns: sorted edge ratios, binned key, canonical order by distance from centroid Brown & Stubis 2017, "TETRA: Star identification with hash tables", AIAA/USU Conference on Small Satellites; tetra3 (ESA, github.com/esa/tetra3) Pattern shape and hash key; pattern-hash hypotheses in the solver crates/fayde-index/src/pattern.rs, crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (pattern_hash) Two-tier index (selection v4): dense verification stars plus greedy brightest-first pattern thinning (ties by ID), minimum separation r_min = 0.6 × fov / sqrt(N), N = pattern_stars_per_fov; pattern membership stored per star (file format v2) ESA tetra3 (generate_database, pattern/verification densities and separation rule); Brown & Stubis 2017 / TETRA About N pattern stars per fov² without coarse-cell brightness artifacts; achieved density depends on input density crates/fayde-index/src/build.rs (select_pattern_stars, pattern_min_sep, build_selected) Lattice fields with a fixed pattern budget, breadth-first brightest-first combinations, prime-sized table, linear probing, 16-bit key check, largest-edge prune, nearest-bin-first lookup cedar-solve (github.com/smroid/cedar-solve, fork of tetra3); no paper Index construction and lookup crates/fayde-index/src/build.rs, pattern.rs, lib.rs (lookup) Multiplicative hashing (constant 2654435761 ≈ 2³²/φ) and linear probing Knuth 1998, The Art of Computer Programming vol. 3, 2nd ed., §6.4 Pattern table addressing crates/fayde-index/src/pattern.rs k-d tree Bentley 1975, Commun. ACM 18(9), 509 Radius searches over star vectors crates/fayde-index/src/kdtree.rs Radius search on a uniform grid of cells (the cell method for fixed-radius near neighbors) Bentley & Friedman 1979, ACM Comput. Surv. 11(4), 397, a survey of range searching in which cells are one of the structures Matching sources to the reference stars of one hypothesis (the points change with every refit, so a structure filled in one pass beats one that is sorted) crates/fayde-solve/src/grid.rs Multiply-rotate hash for keys that are already numbers ("Fx hash") Firefox, and the Rust compiler's rustc-hash crate; no paper Hash maps keyed by grid cells and star identities, in place of SipHash crates/fayde-solve/src/hash.rs Bayesian log-odds verification (true star vs distractor mixture, unique reference claims, ranked sources) Lang et al. 2010, AJ 139, 1782, §2.4 Accepting or rejecting a hypothesis crates/fayde-solve/src/verify.rs Score = largest cumulative log-odds over prefixes of the ranked list; the stars a hypothesis was built from are matched but not scored astrometry.net solver/verify.c (keeps the best index; takes the quad's stars out of its lists), the bestlogodds loop, and the quad's stars moved out of the test list. The prefix maximum is the quantity Ville's maximal inequality bounds for a non-negative supermartingale: Ville 1939, Étude critique de la notion de collectif Source lists with many faint false detections; no evidence from matches that hold by construction crates/fayde-solve/src/verify.rs Pair-separation list with range lookup (k-vector idea; binary search instead of the k-vector's linear interpolation). The pairs are put in bins by squared chord length, and a bin's separations are worked out and sorted when a lookup first reaches it: a lookup returns what the fully sorted list would Mortari 1997, J. Astronaut. Sci. 45(2); Mortari & Neta 2000, AAS 00-128; the bins and the deferred sort are Fayde's Pair seeds for hinted solving crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (PairTable) Progressive sampling: seeds from the best-ranked sources first, ranking by p_star × flux Chum & Matas 2005, CVPR (PROSAC); the scale-prior ordering below is a Fayde extension Source ordering, seed order crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs Local optimization: re-match and refit each promising hypothesis before scoring Chum, Matas & Kittler 2003, DAGM, LNCS 2781 (LO-RANSAC) local_refit crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs Number of false alarms; threshold on log-odds − ln(hypotheses tested) Desolneux, Moisan & Morel 2000 (a-contrario); Moisan & Stival 2004, IJCV 57(3) Acceptance that does not loosen as the search grows crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs Similarity seeds from 2 or 4 correspondences: closed-form complex least squares, z_c = α z_p + β or α conj(z_p) + β, starting in the catalog-centroid tangent plane and refitted with the tangent point at the fitted CRVAL (see Fayde's own choices) Planar equivalent of Umeyama 1991, IEEE TPAMI 13(4), 376–380 (least-squares similarity); related rotation fit: Kabsch 1976, Acta Cryst. A32, 922 Rotation, isotropic scale, translation and both parities without affine shear; also local refits with fewer than 8 matches crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (similarity_seed, rematch_fit) Cauchy IRLS weights 1 / (σ_tot² (1 + (r/r0)²)), source and catalog variance added in quadrature Holland & Welsch 1977, Commun. Stat. 6(9); r0 = 3 σ_tot is Fayde's tuning choice Robust local refits before verification crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (local_refit) IRLS with mixture-model inlier probabilities as weights Holland & Welsch 1977, Commun. Stat. 6(9); Hogg, Bovy & Lang 2010, arXiv:1008.4686 Final WCS fit crates/fayde-solve/src/fit.rs, solve.rs (final_fit) Error-scale factor (reduced χ², Birge ratio) Birge 1932, Phys. Rev. 40, 207 Calibrates default centroid errors and detects under-reported producer errors; per-source floors are a Fayde choice below crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (final_fit) SIP distortion convention (A, B, AP, BP) Shupe et al. 2005, ASP Conf. Ser. 347, 491 Distortion model, FITS cards crates/fayde-wcs/src/sip.rs Distortion fit as a full polynomial in the tangent plane, decomposed into CD + SIP Lang et al. 2010 (astrometry.net tweak) Final fit at order ≥ 2 crates/fayde-solve/src/fit.rs (fit_poly) Model order by BIC with noise variance profiled out: n·ln(χ²/n) + k·ln n, n = 2 Σ inlier_prob, k = 2 × polynomial terms Schwarz 1978, Ann. Stat. 6(2), 461; soft effective sample size is a Fayde choice Choosing TAN vs SIP order 2–3 independently of a common centroid-sigma rescaling crates/fayde-solve/src/fit.rs (fit_best_order) Scale and roll priors as terms of the final fit: a Gaussian prior on a linear-model parameter as one more weighted observation Gelman et al. 2013, Bayesian Data Analysis 3rd ed., ch. 14 (prior information as additional data points); the linearization along CD₀ and ∂CD₀/∂θ, leaving skew and anisotropy free, is Fayde's Holding sparse (5–15 star) fits near the instrument scale and roll crates/fayde-solve/src/fit.rs (LinearPrior, solve_with_prior), solve.rs (linear_prior) Parameter covariance of weighted least squares, (AᵀWA)⁻¹ scaled by the reduced χ² Press et al. 2007, Numerical Recipes 3rd ed., §15.4 Solution::covariance, predicted position errors crates/fayde-solve/src/fit.rs (WcsCovariance) Index series in scale bands (√2 field-size steps), best-matched band first Lang et al. 2010, AJ 139, 1782 Blind solving across unknown pixel scales crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (solve_with_indexes) FITS file structure, binary tables (TFORMn, big-endian), header-only WCS files Pence et al. 2010, A&A 524, A42 (FITS 3.0); IAU FITS Working Group 2016, FITS Standard 4.0 Reading source lists, images and headers, writing source lists and .wcs crates/fayde-fits/src/lib.rs, sources.rs, image.rs Source-list format (frame.sources.fits): a FITS binary table with X/Y in FITS pixels, optional FLUX, SIGMA/SIGMA_PX, P_STAR, TRUNCATED, and IMAGEW/IMAGEH Fayde's own (docs/source-list.md). The X/Y columns and IMAGEW/IMAGEH match the tables astrometry.net reads and writes (Lang et al. 2010), so those files read unchanged Input from any detector; output of fayde detect crates/fayde-fits/src/sources.rs Civil date → day number Hinnant, "chrono-compatible low-level date algorithms" (2013, howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html) DATE-OBS → MJD crates/fayde-fits/src/priors.rs (mjd_from_iso) FNV-1a 64-bit hash Fowler, Noll & Vo; Noll, Vo, Eastlake & Hansen 2026, RFC 9923 Index content hash for provenance and corruption checks crates/fayde-index/src/file.rs Trail census, first estimate: one vote per bright connected component, direction and length √(12·(λmajor − λminor)) from its flux-weighted second moments, weights capped, modes of a histogram of 2θ, weighted medians Danescu & Turcu 2026, Sensors 26(5), 1628 (median orientation and length of elongated components); the moment estimator is Fayde's own Deciding whether a frame's stars are trails, and the trail to start from crates/fayde-detect/src/trail.rs (components, census) Aimed segment filter: running sums along sheared rows (lines of the trail's direction made rows, linear interpolation across them), window weights summing to the physical length, then the point detector's Gaussian Scanning every translate of a digital line at any angle: Soille, Breen & Jones 1996, IEEE TPAMI 18(5), 562 (for erosion and dilation; using the scan for running sums is Fayde's); the matched filter for a trail is the PSF convolved with the segment: Nir, Zackay & Ofek 2018, AJ 156, 229 Finding trails at about √(L / 1.5 FWHM) times the point filter's signal-to-noise ratio crates/fayde-detect/src/trail.rs (aimed_box, line_sums) Threshold for the aimed filter: the Gaussian kernel with the same density of noise maxima, σ² = 1 / (2√det Λ), Λ the gradient covariance of the actual kernel on a quarter-pixel grid Adler & Taylor 2007, Random Fields and Geometry (density of maxima of a smooth Gaussian field) One noise peak per frame in the trail filter, as in the point filter crates/fayde-detect/src/trail.rs (equivalent_sigma) Trail fit: pixel-integrated Gaussian ⊛ segment (erf model), the frame's length, angle and width held, position, flux and a background plane free; Gauss–Newton; errors along and across from the Fisher matrix; trail against point by the likelihood ratio (equal parameter counts, geometry known) Vereš et al. 2012, PASP 124, 1197; Bouquillon et al. 2017, A&A 606, A27 (model and Cramér–Rao bounds) Each star trail's position and its errors along and across crates/fayde-detect/src/trail.rs (profile, fit) Neighbors' models subtracted before a second fit Neighbor-subtracted PSF fitting: Stetson 1987, PASP 99, 191 (DAOPHOT) Trails beside or in line with one another crates/fayde-detect/src/trail.rs (run) Empirical PSF from isolated stars, registered and combined with a clipped mean Empirical PSF from isolated stars: Stetson 1987, PASP 99, 191 (DAOPHOT), Bertin 2011, ASP Conf. Ser. 442, 435 (PSFEx). The clipped mean (each pixel of the stack leaves out values farther than 4 × (noise + 5% of the median) from the median, and weights the rest by inverse variance), the cutoff on template bend and the regional model for field rotation are Fayde's. Shared curved paths and field rotation crates/fayde-detect/src/kernel.rs (train), kernel/rotation.rs (Rotation::learn) Local cubic interpolation Catmull & Rom 1974, Computer Aided Geometric Design, 317 Subpixel registration and translation of the empirical template crates/fayde-detect/src/kernel.rs (cubic, sample) Direct matched filter with a sparse template; suppress sidelobes by subtracting brighter fitted sources before correlating again Zackay & Ofek 2017, ApJ 836, 187 (matched filter); Högbom 1974, A&AS 15, 417 (CLEAN-style subtraction). Fayde subtracts sources in image space and checks the correlation at each candidate. Finding and separating stars smeared by curved motion crates/fayde-detect/src/kernel.rs (correlate, measure) Empirical template fit and position covariance; density of noise peaks from the template gradient covariance Bouquillon et al. 2017, A&A 606, A27 (Fisher information); Adler & Taylor 2007, Random Fields and Geometry (noise-peak density); Efron 2008, Stat. Sci. 23(1), 1 (local false discovery rate) Positions, errors, thresholds, and star probabilities crates/fayde-detect/src/kernel.rs (fit, measure, Template::equivalent_sigma) Regional rotation templates with an empirical transverse profile and a Gaussian-smoothed segment along the local tangent Gaussian-smoothed segment from Vereš et al. 2012, PASP 124, 1197. Fayde fits the rotation center and angular span, and uses a quadratic arc along the segment. Detection at varying trail lengths and directions in a rotating field crates/fayde-detect/src/kernel/rotation.rs (Rotation::template) Charge-transfer smear: traps release charge behind the packet, so a source is displaced away from the readout, more for faint sources and more transfers, growing with radiation dose Physics: Janesick 2001, Scientific Charge-Coupled Devices, SPIE Press (charge-transfer efficiency and traps). The astrometric effect on faint against bright sources and its growth with time: Anderson & Bedin 2010, PASP 122, 1035; Massey et al. 2010, MNRAS 401, 371. The model, shift = s(t) · (transfers / 1000) · max(0, ln(flux_ref / F)) with s(t) = max(0, shift_px + per_year · (t − epoch)), is Fayde's own, chosen from Fayde's residuals on real frames from one camera (after correction, faint against bright within 0.05 px per 1000 rows over 300 to 64,000 flux units; the frames are not in the repository) Correcting detected positions with an instrument profile crates/fayde-fits/src/instrument.rs (ChargeTransfer), crates/fayde-api/src/lib.rs (detect_sources) Periodic background pattern removed: in 32 × 32 pixel tiles, the offset and a cosine and a sine term per known frequency fitted by least squares to the pixels away from sources (3 robust σ from the tile median, 2 px around), the terms interpolated bilinearly between tile centers and the waves subtracted Least-squares fitting of sinusoids to unevenly sampled data: Lomb 1976, Ap&SS 39, 447; Scargle 1982, ApJ 263, 835. Tiled fits that follow a slowly drifting amplitude and phase are Fayde's own Readout stripes, before detection with a profile or during the trail census retry crates/fayde-detect/src/pattern.rs (remove), crates/fayde-api/src/lib.rs (detect_sources), crates/fayde-detect/src/trail.rs (clean_census) Periodic pattern frequencies: power spectra of the frames' backgrounds (sources clipped) on a power-of-two square by a radix-2 fast Fourier transform, normalized and averaged; peaks 30 times the median power holding at least 0.5% of the variance, refined between bins by a parabola through the log power Cooley & Tukey 1965, Math. Comp. 19, 297. Peak thresholds are Fayde's own fayde calibrate --periodic-pattern and single-frame trail census retry (waves with at least 2% power and two cycles per fitting tile) crates/fayde-detect/src/pattern.rs (Finder), crates/fayde-detect/src/trail.rs (clean_census) Charge-transfer calibration: each frame's offset and linear terms projected out of the residuals frame by frame, then one least-squares fit of the shift (and its rate per year) for each of the four readout geometries, 5σ clipping on the robust spread; the four compared on one set of stars, and the term kept from those whose shift is positive and at least 5σ Partitioned regression: Frisch & Waugh 1933, Econometrica 1(4), 387; Lovell 1963, JASA 58, 993. Median absolute deviation: Hampel 1974 fayde calibrate --charge-transfer crates/fayde-api/src/calibrate.rs (calibrate_charge_transfer)

The detection entries (fayde-detect) come from the survey in the literature review, §7 and §8, which say how much of each source was read.

docs.title: Fayde's own choices (no published source)
docs.text: Choice Rationale Code Incremental Cartesian unit-vector buckets of side at least the separation chord, searching 27 neighboring buckets and checking exact distances Bounded local searches for streaming insertion/replacement and pattern thinning, without rebuilding the static k-d tree; independent of HEALPix boundaries crates/fayde-index/src/build.rs (SeparationGrid) High-proper-motion cut: drop a star from patterns if |μ| × 25 yr > 0.5 × pattern_max_error × fov/2 A shift δ changes ratios by ≈ δ / (largest edge); keeps motion-induced ratio error within half a bin over the index lifetime crates/fayde-index/src/build.rs Default proper-motion error 50 mas/yr where UCAC4 has none Value UCAC4 itself uses for "no data" in output tables (readme note 9) crates/fayde-catalog/src/ucac4.rs Strict-by-default catalog queries (missing zone = error) An empty cone must never be mistaken for empty sky crates/fayde-catalog/src/lib.rs Pre-filter: ≥ 2 of the next 12 ranked sources must land on seed-list catalog stars within 3σ + 2 px + 1% of distance from the seed pair Tolerance grows with distance because a 2-star seed's rotation/scale error does crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (prefilter) Reference count per hypothesis: brightest clamp(round(1.5 × Σ p_star), 10, 2000) catalog stars in the frame, using usable sources after duplicate demotion (p_star defaults to 1) Effective real-source count prevents low-probability detections from inflating background density; placeholder until detection_limit is supported (design doc §6.2) crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs Local-refit radii 12 → 6 → 3 px; similarity fit below 8 matches, affine from 8 Tuned on synthetic fields; four to seven stars cannot constrain shear and anisotropy crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (local_refit, rematch_fit) A polynomial order above 1 is a BIC candidate only with four observations per parameter, n ≥ 4k (24 matches for order 2, 40 for order 3); n ≥ 2k while a tune-up is still collecting matches, whose result is refitted under the strict rule The profiled BIC has no floor: as k approaches n the fit interpolates, χ² → 0 and n·ln(χ²/n) → −∞. Measured without a rule, hinted solves of sparse frames: 43 of 60 frames with 6 stars and 52 of 60 with 10 stars returned a WCS wrong by ≥ 15″ at the corners. Short of interpolation it stays too liberal with outliers among a few dozen matches: on 1,200 undistorted frames of 12–50 stars, n ≥ 2k chose distortion 16 times (corner errors up to 107″), n ≥ 3k 5 times, n ≥ 4k once (3″); a BIC margin of up to 50 instead of a count still left 3 crates/fayde-solve/src/fit.rs (fit_best_order) Similarity fits are repeated with the tangent point moved to the fitted CRVAL until it stops moving A transform found in another point's tangent plane is rotated by (east offset × tan δ) at CRVAL (convergence of the meridians). Measured: median hypotheses per hinted solve at Dec 86–89° fell from 607 to 6, the same as at low declination crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (similarity_seed) Distortion tune-up: a hypothesis that is not conclusive under a linear model, or that matches over 1.25× (+3) as many stars at 12 px as inside its own gates, is re-matched at 12 px with the order chosen by BIC until no more stars join, then at 6 and 3 px; the better-scoring of the linear and tuned models is kept, and the tune-up counts as one more hypothesis Fayde's own. With lens distortion a linear model leaves the outer stars outside the match gate. astrometry.net also refits a promising match before deciding (the tune-up in solver_handle_hit, solver.c, which refits at order 1), without distortion. Measured: 5% distortion with 0.3 px centroids went from 18/30 solved (4 of them wrong by > 3″) to 30/30, none wrong crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (tune, try_hypothesis) A distortion polynomial is kept only if its confident matches cover the sources: in a 3 × 3 grid, every cell with ≥ 6 sources must have a matched fraction ≥ 0.25 × the frame's overall matched fraction; otherwise TAN, or no solution if the hypothesis only passed with distortion A polynomial locked onto part of the frame was wrong by up to 80 px in the rest (10% distortion test). Good fits had a lowest cell ratio of 0.47, partial locks ≤ 0.13 crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (covers_sources, final_fit) The fitted WCS must itself clear the acceptance threshold; the final IRLS runs until the match set and error scale repeat (at most 20 iterations, at least 4) The returned solution should be the one that passed, at a converged fit crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (final_fit) SIP inverse AP/BP of order forward + 2, fitted on a 25×25 grid; Fayde itself inverts by fixed-point iteration on A/B (exact to 1e-10 px) A quartic leaves 0.03 px at the corners of a cubic barrel; order + 2 gives < 0.01 px for external FITS readers crates/fayde-wcs/src/sip.rs Settle the match set with two TAN iterations before letting BIC consider SIP Avoids fitting distortion to a match set chosen by a wrong model crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (final_fit) A distortion order is kept only if no lower order predicts held-out cells of the frame (3 × 3, each left out in turn, training sets at n ≥ 2k) within 5% of its squared error; the lowest such order is used. Matches in fewer than 4 cells allow no distortion; when the order itself cannot be scored, BIC's order stands Spatial block cross-validation: Roberts et al. 2017, Ecography 40, 913. On simulated undistorted frames whose matches carry errors in one region, BIC took order 3 and the polynomial ran up to 146 px off in the corners crates/fayde-solve/src/fit.rs (held_out_order), crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (supported_order) When the request has a scale or roll prior, a final fit that ends with distortion is converged again as TAN with scale and roll free of the priors, matching afresh. Both are scored on the same sources at the distortion fit's error scale. A TAN outside the hint's hard limits replaces the distortion fit if it explains the sources at least as well (the hard limits then refuse it); a TAN inside them replaces it only with higher posterior odds, priors included Fayde's own. With the hint's scale wrong by more than its limits, the scale stopped inside them and distortion made up the rest with partly wrong matches (42.7 px off in the corners, log-odds 394); a trailed frame with smear did the same (30.7 px). With both checks the first gives no solution and the second solves to 0.03 px; of 106 simulated frames solved with distortion, 8 more are correct and none worse; 178 of 186 real-frame solutions stay bit-identical and the other 8 move closer to the Gaia references crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (converge) Header priors order: XPIXSZ/FOCALLEN, then a unit-checked linear WCS (CD, or PC × CDELT), then PIXSCALE/SECPIX; headers with both CD and PC give no scale; pointing from CRVAL then RA/DEC then OBJCTRA/OBJCTDEC; time from JD-OBS, MJD-OBS, then DATE-OBS (+TIME-OBS), all + EXPTIME/2 for mid-exposure No published source; CUNIT = 'degree(s)' accepted alongside FITS deg because some real headers use it crates/fayde-fits/src/priors.rs Tangent-plane inverse defined for every input: beyond 1e150 rad the reference-point term is dropped and only the direction of the offset is kept (the limit of the gnomonic inverse, 90° from the reference point); a NaN offset gives the reference point A WCS or pixel at the edge of the f64 range gave a panic; the limit is the mathematically defined answer crates/fayde-wcs/src/tan.rs (Basis::deproject) Header numbers must be finite: NaN, inf and exponents past the f64 range are kept as text, so a numeric read of that keyword is an error naming it A non-finite WCS or SIP value must not reach the arithmetic, and must not be read as an absent term crates/fayde-wcs/src/header.rs (parse_value), crates/fayde-wcs/src/sip.rs Repeated keyword: the first card is the one looked up Matches the lookup of cfitsio and Astropy, so a header that repeats a keyword gives the same WCS in each crates/fayde-wcs/src/header.rs (Header::get) Plausible epoch range, Julian years 1800 to 2200: a header clock outside it is reported and skipped, a request or index epoch outside it is an error A Julian Date in MJD-OBS or an unset camera clock otherwise moves every star by centuries of proper motion and fails with an unrelated message crates/fayde-core/src/epoch.rs, crates/fayde-fits/src/priors.rs, crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (validate) Header pointing is used only when the header does not declare another frame: RADESYS other than ICRS or FK5, or EQUINOX other than 2000, drops it with a warning (a bare EPOCH is not consulted: it is also written for the observation date); right ascension outside [0°, 360°) or 24 h is rejected, not wrapped No precession is applied, so B1950 or equinox-of-date coordinates are up to about 0.7° from ICRS; a prior must not be those coordinates read as ICRS crates/fayde-fits/src/priors.rs (foreign_frame, header_priors) Blind hypotheses whose implied frame exceeds twice the index field size are skipped before any catalog query An index cannot hold patterns larger than its fields; such hypotheses produced sky-sized cones (found in a comparison run on real frames) crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (pattern_hash) Catalog cones cached per (HEALPix cell of the field center, √2 field-radius bucket) Avoids one catalog query per blind hypothesis crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (pattern_hash) Catalog stars of a pointing prior read as hypotheses need them: only the brightest stars of the prior's cone for seeding (Catalog::cone_brightest), and every star in a cone of 1.25 × the frame's radius around a hypothesis that passes the pre-filter; after 6 such reads the rest of the prior's cone is read in one go A 2° prior around a 0.6° frame covers 46 frame areas, and reading, propagating and sorting all of it was three quarters of a hinted solve. A hypothesis sees the stars it would see with the whole cone in memory, in the same order: results on 109 real frames are unchanged to the last bit. Of those solves, 62 needed one read and 1 the whole cone crates/fayde-solve/src/refset.rs, solve.rs (pair_seeds, prior_cone) Cone test that computes the exact separation only at the edge: a star whose J2000 direction is farther from the center than the radius plus the largest proper motion is rejected on a dot product; the others are decided by the chord from the vector the propagation produced, and centre.separation(position) > radius is evaluated only within 1e-9 rad of the edge (and for cones wider than 1 rad) The exact form costs two sines, two cosines and an arctangent per star on top of the propagation. Compared with a record-by-record scan: 1.7 million stars in 720 cones equal, including 5,565 cones whose edge passes through or beside a star crates/fayde-catalog/src/ucac4.rs (ConeTest) Pair seeds within 3σ of the pointing before the whole prior cone, when 3σ is at most half the hard radius A pointing is usually known far better than the limit set on it, and the work of a pair-seed stage grows with its cone's area. 3σ holds 98.9% of a two-dimensional Gaussian. The first look is skipped when it would be more than half the limit (the default σ is a quarter of it): it would then cost nearly as much as the search it spares, and a frame it cannot solve would pay twice. Measured on 146 real source lists: 8.7 ms per list at a 2° limit, 1.1 ms at 0.25° crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (plan, pair_seeds) Instrument profile from solved frames (fayde calibrate): median fitted scale, with 1σ = 1.5 × its robust spread and at least 0.1% of the scale; parity when every solution agrees; roll rule offset + sign × keyword for the sign whose offsets scatter less, offset the median about the mean direction, 1σ = 2 × the robust spread (at least 0.05°), hard limit 10σ (at least 1°); pointing 1σ = median offset between the header pointing and the solved frame center, divided by √(2 ln 2) Medians and median absolute deviations, so that poor solutions among the frames do not move the profile. The 0.1% floor: the solver's hard limit is 3σ on the scale fitted to one frame, and fits to a dozen stars scatter by 0.1 to 0.2% (a σ of 0.04% of the scale lost a frame). √(2 ln 2) is the median of a Rayleigh distribution in units of its σ: the radial offset of a pointing with a Gaussian error σ per axis. A profile needs no other solver: 66 of Fayde's own solutions gave a roll scatter of 0.039° crates/fayde-api/src/calibrate.rs Header read without its WCS (--no-header-wcs, profile header_wcs: false): the cards of a world coordinate system are dropped before the priors are read, so the pointing comes from RA/DEC or OBJCTRA/OBJCTDEC and no scale from CD or CDELT A header WCS may be another plate solver's solution, which a test of Fayde alone must not use and which later frames may not have crates/fayde-wcs/src/header.rs (without_wcs), crates/fayde-api/src/lib.rs (build_request) Cone search without u4index.unf: binary search of each zone file by RA; the records it leads to are checked for RA order A catalog copy without u4i/ read whole zones: 350 ms per hinted solve, where a copy with the index took 22 ms. The search reads the records the index gives (see the UCAC4 entry above) crates/fayde-catalog/src/ucac4.rs (ra_range) Pattern search depth: top 16 ranked sources, breadth-first Dense synthetic fields abstained with 10 (all-sky benchmark); breadth-first order keeps the cost on frames the smaller depth could not solve crates/fayde-solve/src/request.rs (Policy::pattern_sources) Adaptive search plan from request metadata (pair seeds / ringed region hash / scale-pruned hash / blind / opt-in out-of-prior), shared hypothesis count across stages Fayde's own crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (plan, solve_auto) Region filter: all 4 pattern stars within (ring radius + implied field radius) of the pointing Rejects off-region hash matches before any fitting crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (pattern_hash) Placeholder scale rejection: a scale implying a field wider than a hemisphere (solver) or than 60° half-diagonal (header reader) Found on cropped frames whose headers carry non-WCS scale values crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (new_ctx), crates/fayde-fits/src/priors.rs Prior terms in the hypothesis score: ln(prior density / uniform density over the hard limits) for pointing (2-D Gaussian vs a cap of the hard radius), scale and roll (1-D Gaussians vs their ranges) Standard Bayesian odds (the same framework as Lang et al. 2010's verification); the uniform-over-limits reference is Fayde's choice crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (prior_log_ratio) Catalog position error at epoch added in quadrature to the centroid error, per match Standard error propagation; uses the catalog's Star::pos_err_mas crates/fayde-solve/src/verify.rs, solve.rs Duplicates: a source within 3 px of a better-ranked one gets p_star × 0.1 and is ranked last Detector fragments otherwise compete for the same reference star crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (new_ctx) Ranking: measured-flux sources by p_star × flux, then sources without flux in input order One missing flux must not discard all flux information crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (new_ctx) Polynomial fits in normalized offsets (u/S, v/S), coefficients rescaled by S^-(p+q) Standard least-squares conditioning (Press et al. 2007, §15.4); a safeguard: tests at 4096 px, orders 3 and 5, matched with and without it crates/fayde-solve/src/fit.rs, crates/fayde-wcs/src/sip.rs Leave-one-out residuals r/(1 − h) with leverage h = w·fᵀ(AᵀWA)⁻¹f; worst predicted σ over a 5×5 grid Hoaglin & Welsch 1978, Am. Stat. 32(1), 17 (the hat matrix); the grid report is Fayde's crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (final_fit), fit.rs (worst_radial_sigma_arcsec) Truncated sources: anisotropic Gaussian gate along the frame trail (1σ = L/2), excluded from fits and seeds Fayde's own crates/fayde-solve/src/verify.rs, solve.rs Instrument profile with a header-keyword roll rule Fayde's own crates/fayde-fits/src/instrument.rs, profiles/example.json verify_wcs / refine_wcs (fayde verify, fayde refit): score an existing WCS; re-match 12 → 6 → 3 px and refit with the solver's IRLS/BIC Fayde's own, reusing Lang et al. 2010 verification crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs Strategy: pair seeds first when there is a pointing prior and σ/scale ≤ 3%, then the pattern hash; the hash alone otherwise (including no priors) Follows the design (§5.3) and the oversampling measurement in §5.2 crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (solve_with_index) Pattern-hash ratio tolerance clamp(8.5σ / L, 0.002, 0.02), L = largest image edge Propagated centroid noise (≈ 2√2σ/L per ratio) × 3 crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (pattern_hash) Pattern-hash assignments: enumerate all ≤ 24 image permutations whose six labeled edge ratios (each divided by the largest edge) agree within lookup tolerance; fit both similarity parities, retain radial RMS ≤ 3 × max source σ, try smallest RMS first; require ≥ 1 extra index-star hit Canonical centroid-distance ranks can swap under noise; the similarity fit is sourced above, while enumeration, thresholds and residual ordering are Fayde choices crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (pattern_seeds, pattern_hash) Hypothesis count starts after hard priors pass; each surviving permutation/parity is a separate trial, including cheap pre-filter failures Hard-prior rejections lie outside the searched model space; retains the NFA penalty for every eligible tested seed crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (pair_seeds, pattern_hash) Catalog pair traversal starts nearest the separation implied by the scale-prior mean, then alternates outward on either side Fayde's prior-guided extension of PROSAC (Chum & Matas 2005); tries plausible scales before the low edge of the permitted interval crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (pairs_from_mean) Default centroid sigma may shrink under the fitted error scale; producer-supplied sigma retains a floor of 1 on its multiplier A policy default is an initial estimate; measured producer errors remain a lower bound, including mixed source lists crates/fayde-solve/src/solve.rs (final_fit), verify.rs (assess) Detection pipeline as a whole: the star width measured from the frame and the filter matched to it (binning wide stars), one closed-form fit per peak supplying position, error, size and shape, classes and probabilities passed on to the solver's verification No detector surveyed (docs/research/literature-review.md §7) adapts its filter to a measured width, reports a per-star position error, or traces streaks before solving crates/fayde-detect/src/lib.rs; docs/design/detection.md Position error of the maximum of a filtered image, σx = σt² / (√2·σk·SNR); photon-noise term σp²·σt⁸ / (N·σk⁴·(σk² + 2σp²)²) Derived (docs/design/detection.md §4): noise gradient over signal curvature. Equal to the Cramér–Rao bound and to Mortensen et al.'s eq. 6 for a matched kernel; on synthetic frames the error over the claim has a robust spread of 0.8 to 1.25 crates/fayde-detect/src/lib.rs (finish) Star width as the widest distinct mode of the size distribution of bright, round peaks (histogram of ln size, bins of 0.25; a mode needs 5% of the tallest and a dip to half below it) Nothing from the sky is sharper than the optics, and stars share one width where hot pixels and cosmic rays have many. A real frame from a warm detector had 300 radiation hits to 36 stars; a median took the hits' width and the frame did not solve crates/fayde-detect/src/lib.rs (measure_psf) Star shape: the frame's narrow-axis variance and axis ratio, medians over the peaks of the star mode; "sharp" is under 0.4 of the narrow-axis variance, "extended" and streak seeds are 1.5 and 2 times the stars' own axis ratio A drift during the exposure smears every star alike. Judged against the mean width, the 36 brightest stars of a real frame smeared two to one were classed as cosmic rays, and the frame did not solve crates/fayde-detect/src/lib.rs (measure_shape, classify), streak.rs Local test: a peak must stand above the median of a ring at three star-widths by the threshold less one σ, where the ring disagrees with the mesh A mesh cannot follow stray light or halos. Synthetic glow of 20 × sky from a corner: 33 false stars without, 1 with crates/fayde-detect/src/lib.rs (stand_out), peaks.rs (ring_median) Mesh tiles replaced only when above the largest of the four two-neighbor line means; straight-line extrapolation of the background beyond the outermost tile centers A 3 × 3 median flattens the corner of a frame lit from outside, and a mesh held flat to the edge turns a gradient into signal (111 false sources at the edge of a binned frame before, 3 after) crates/fayde-detect/src/mesh.rs (despike, at) Detection threshold as min(pixel tail, peak density) for a number of noise peaks per frame (default 1) A maximum above u on pixels is a pixel above u, so the pixel count bounds the continuous-field density where that overshoots (narrow kernels). Counted on empty frames: within 45% for σk 0.7 to 2 px crates/fayde-detect/src/stats.rs Classes and their limits: sharp under 0.4 of the stars' variance; extended over 2 × or elongated over 1.5, each beyond 2.5 × the fit's error 2/SNR; class factors on p_star of 0.9 (saturated) and 0.5 (extended) Tuned on synthetic frames. The error of a fitted minor-axis variance was measured at 0.9 to 1.6 /SNR of the total with a bias of −1.3/SNR crates/fayde-detect/src/lib.rs (classify) Saturation level from flat-topped peaks at the frame's brightest level; center of a saturated star from the core of its saturated region (pixels with long runs along both axes); error 0.1 px + 3% of the core radius A bleed trail has short runs across it; a flat top below the brightest level is a cosmic-ray track or a stuck column. Measured: center within 0.6 px for stars 3 to 300 × saturation with trails crates/fayde-detect/src/saturate.rs, lib.rs (find_saturation) Streak tracing: seeds from ridge-like peaks (elongation ≥ 2), a walk along a running least-squares line (search ± 2 px, threshold 3σ, gaps of 8 px + 10% of the points, at most 30), end clean-up, total-least-squares line, half-level ends, a second trace from the fitted line, acceptance (10 px and 8σ long, half covered, SNR 10, half of the bright peaks ridges), cosmic_ray when narrower than 0.4 of the stars' variance Fayde's own; a line model through the walk keeps it on course across a crossing streak. Measured: ends within 2 px, 0.2 px typical crates/fayde-detect/src/streak.rs Census, second estimate: autocovariance of the filtered image, each anchor counted once (partner over anchor, at most 2), saturated stars and traced satellite streaks left out; on a retry, anchors from bright elongated components across all directions; direction coarse to fine (36 directions at a lag of four widths, then the lag doubled up to half a trail, two correlation widths searched each time); length from a PSF-blurred triangle plus a constant. It must agree with the first estimate within 20% in length and three filtered widths over the length (at least 4.6°) in direction, and the trail must be the same in each region of a 3 × 3 grid with enough trails, else in the trails fitted one by one Fayde's own (docs/design/streak-detection.md §4.1, §7). Loose in direction: on real frames its direction was off by up to 5° where the first estimate was within 0.5° of the fits; it guards against gross failures (merged blobs, bleed trails), and the filter is aimed by the fits crates/fayde-detect/src/trail.rs (autocovariance, census, run) Trails shorter than 7 FWHM (across the trail) are left to the point detector Real frames meant to show points drift by up to 6.8 FWHM, and the point pass solves them; the point filter loses under 0.2 mag at 2 FWHM crates/fayde-detect/src/trail.rs (MIN_LENGTH_FWHM) A frame with more than four round sources of the stars' width per trail vote is refused Point stars with a few aligned satellite segments must not pass as trailed;
